title: NYT 100 Best TV Shows of the 21st Century
source: New York Times industry poll (Sep 2026); shows premiered on/after 2000-01-01
owner_flags_note: status/notes are Nate Beyor's Personal Admin checklist as of 2026-09-27; only ranks 1-20 decided; 21-100 still unchecked

shows.title: Breaking Bad
shows.description: A New Mexico chemistry teacher with cancer turns to cooking meth to secure his family's future.
shows.reviewPro: Moral free-fall this precise is rare; the performances and plotting stay airtight.
shows.reviewCon: The early episodes take their time, and the violence is not gentle.

shows.title: The Wire
shows.description: An ensemble crime epic that maps Baltimore through cops, dealers, schools, politics, and the press.
shows.reviewPro: The richest portrait of a city on television, with institutions as the real villain.
shows.reviewCon: It asks for patience; the slang and the sprawl can feel impenetrable at first.

shows.title: Mad Men
shows.description: 1960s Madison Avenue ad men chase clients, status, and identity as America remakes itself.
shows.reviewPro: Gorgeous, precise writing about identity, ambition, and American self-invention.
shows.reviewCon: Slow, interior, and often chilly. Plot matters less than mood and manners.

shows.title: Succession
shows.description: A media dynasty's heirs claw for control as their ruthless father refuses to let go.
shows.reviewPro: Vicious, quotable family warfare, with a cast operating at full power.
shows.reviewCon: Almost nobody is likable, and the cruelty is the point for hours on end.

shows.title: Fleabag
shows.description: A wry London woman breaks the fourth wall while navigating grief, desire, and family chaos.
shows.reviewPro: Two short seasons of grief, desire, and fourth-wall jokes that actually cut.
shows.reviewCon: The pain under the jokes gets heavy. It is a short, intense sit.

shows.title: Game of Thrones
shows.description: Noble houses battle for the Iron Throne in a fantasy world of betrayal, dragons, and winter.
shows.reviewPro: The early seasons are sprawling, shocking fantasy with a huge sense of scale.
shows.reviewCon: The final stretch is widely considered a rushed, unsatisfying landing.

shows.title: Veep
shows.description: A foul-mouthed U.S. vice president and her staff scramble through political farce and failure.
shows.reviewPro: The sharpest political farce on TV. The insults are engineering.
shows.reviewCon: Relentless cynicism. If you want warmth, look elsewhere.

shows.title: 30 Rock
shows.description: A sketch-show showrunner juggles NBC chaos, eccentric stars, and corporate absurdity.
shows.reviewPro: Joke density this high is a magic trick, and the ensemble never misses.
shows.reviewCon: Chaos is the style. Continuity and sincerity are not the point.

shows.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm
shows.description: Larry David plays a heightened version of himself, turning social etiquette into endless conflict.
shows.reviewPro: Social discomfort as high art. Larry David's timing is still unmatched.
shows.reviewCon: Cringe is the engine. Many scenes are built to make you squirm.

shows.title: Atlanta
shows.description: A Princeton dropout manages his cousin's rap career in a surreal, sharp portrait of Black Atlanta.
shows.reviewPro: Surreal, funny, and formally daring, with episodes that feel like short films.
shows.reviewCon: The anthology swings can feel disjointed if you want one straight plot.
shows.notes: Mostly seen; Nate would finish, Jen would not

shows.title: The Office (U.S.)
shows.description: A mockumentary about the awkward staff of a Scranton paper company and their clueless boss.
shows.reviewPro: A comfort-watch ensemble that turned awkwardness into real affection.
shows.reviewCon: Early Michael is hard to watch, and the later seasons thin out.

shows.title: Arrested Development
shows.description: A wealthy family collapses into schemes and secrets after the patriarch is jailed for fraud.
shows.reviewPro: The densest callback comedy ever made. The first three seasons repay rewatches.
shows.reviewCon: The later revival seasons are spottier and lose the original snap.

shows.title: Girls
shows.description: Four young women in New York stumble through work, sex, friendship, and growing up.
shows.reviewPro: A frank, specific portrait of messy twentysomething friendship in New York.
shows.reviewCon: The leads are often selfish on purpose, which alienates plenty of viewers.

shows.title: Friday Night Lights
shows.description: A Texas high-school football town lives and breathes every Friday under the lights.
shows.reviewPro: Earnest, big-hearted drama that makes a football town feel like a family.
shows.reviewCon: The sports frame and the Texas sincerity are not for everyone.

shows.title: Six Feet Under
shows.description: A dysfunctional L.A. funeral-home family grapples with death, love, and who they want to be.
shows.reviewPro: Funny and profound about family, grief, and how to live with death.
shows.reviewCon: Family misery is the subject. It can feel heavy week after week.

shows.title: The Office (U.K.)
shows.description: Ricky Gervais's original mockumentary about a bleak British office and its desperate manager.
shows.reviewPro: The original cringe masterpiece: short, bleak, and painfully well observed.
shows.reviewCon: Meaner and sadder than the U.S. version, with very little relief.

shows.title: The Americans
shows.description: Two Soviet spies pose as a suburban American couple while raising kids who don't know the truth.
shows.reviewPro: A marriage thriller that gets richer as the lies compound. Quietly devastating.
shows.reviewCon: Deliberate pacing: spy craft and domestic dread, not action set pieces.

shows.title: I May Destroy You
shows.description: A writer rebuilds her life and art after a sexual assault she can't fully remember.
shows.reviewPro: Bold and formally alive, about memory, consent, and making art after harm.
shows.reviewCon: The subject is sexual assault. It is frank, fragmented, and heavy.

shows.title: Chernobyl
shows.description: A limited series on the 1986 nuclear disaster and the covers-ups that made it worse.
shows.reviewPro: Five tight episodes of dread, procedure, and moral courage. Remarkably controlled.
shows.reviewCon: Grim by design. The disaster and the cover-up leave little air.

shows.title: The Crown
shows.description: A dramatized chronicle of Queen Elizabeth II's reign and the private costs of public duty.
shows.reviewPro: Lavish and well cast, it makes public duty feel like a private tragedy.
shows.reviewCon: Later seasons draw more debate about accuracy, and the tone stays solemn.

shows.title: The White Lotus
shows.description: Vacationers at a luxury resort collide in dark comedy about class, privilege, and desire.
shows.reviewPro: Acid social satire in beautiful places. Each season is a self-contained bite.
shows.reviewCon: The guests are awful on purpose, and the mystery can outrank the people.

shows.title: Lost
shows.description: Plane-crash survivors on a mysterious island face monsters, flashbacks, and each other.
shows.reviewPro: Peak mystery-box television: character, cliffhangers, and a huge ensemble.
shows.reviewCon: The mythology outruns the answers. The ending still divides people.

shows.title: The Comeback
shows.description: A faded sitcom star claws back into Hollywood in a cringe-comedy of fame and humiliation.
shows.reviewPro: Cringe comedy with a real point about fame, age, and who gets to be seen.
shows.reviewCon: The heroine is excruciating by design. Humiliation is the joke.

shows.title: Deadwood
shows.description: A lawless Dakota gold camp builds itself into a town through violence, deals, and dirty talk.
shows.reviewPro: Shakespearean swearing in a mud street. The dialogue is the special effect.
shows.reviewCon: Dense, profane, and unfinished on its own terms until a later movie.

shows.title: The Leftovers
shows.description: After 2% of the world's people vanish, the leftover struggle with faith, grief, and meaning.
shows.reviewPro: Grief science fiction that becomes one of the most moving shows of its era.
shows.reviewCon: The first season is deliberately miserable. Faith and ambiguity are the plot.

shows.title: Black Mirror
shows.description: Anthology stories about technology's dark, twisted edges and what we do with it.
shows.reviewPro: A cultural shorthand for tech anxiety, with several genuinely great hours.
shows.reviewCon: Anthology quality swings hard, and the cynicism can feel samey.

shows.title: Better Call Saul
shows.description: Jimmy McGill's slow-burn transformation into criminal lawyer Saul Goodman before Breaking Bad.
shows.reviewPro: A patient character tragedy that many people think outgrows Breaking Bad.
shows.reviewCon: It is a slow burn for a long time. Action fans may bounce early.

shows.title: Band of Brothers
shows.description: A WWII miniseries following Easy Company from training through Europe to war's end.
shows.reviewPro: The standard for World War II miniseries: scale, brotherhood, and craft.
shows.reviewCon: The combat is intense, and a large cast of similar faces can blur.

shows.title: Key & Peele
shows.description: Sketch comedy that skewers race, politics, and pop culture with surgical absurdity.
shows.reviewPro: Sketch precision with a point of view. The hits became instant canon.
shows.reviewCon: Like any sketch show, some premises die in the first thirty seconds.

shows.title: Severance
shows.description: Office workers surgically split work and home selves, then start asking what the company hides.
shows.reviewPro: A clean, eerie premise about work and the self, directed with real style.
shows.reviewCon: It withholds answers. If you need the mystery to pay off fast, you may fidget.

shows.title: Survivor
shows.description: Castaways compete in challenges and alliances until one is the sole survivor.
shows.reviewPro: The reality format that still works: strategy, personalities, and camp life.
shows.reviewCon: Two decades of seasons means a lot of repetition if you try to binge it all.

shows.title: Andor
shows.description: A Star Wars spy thriller about how ordinary people become rebels against the Empire.
shows.reviewPro: The rare franchise show that is actually about politics, sacrifice, and craft.
shows.reviewCon: Slower and talkier than typical Star Wars. That is the bet.

shows.title: Enlightened
shows.description: A corporate whistleblower tries to remake her life and company after a very public meltdown.
shows.reviewPro: A sharp, tender comedy about wanting to be good inside a rotten company.
shows.reviewCon: The heroine is embarrassing on purpose. Short, and still underseen.

shows.title: Schitt's Creek
shows.description: A rich family loses everything and rebuilds in a tiny town they once bought as a joke.
shows.reviewPro: A warm redemption that earns its sweetness without going soft too fast.
shows.reviewCon: The early snob comedy is broad. The glow comes later.

shows.title: True Detective (Season 1)
shows.description: Two Louisiana detectives hunt a ritual killer across years of obsession and damaged lives.
shows.reviewPro: A humid, hypnotic detective story with two performances for the ages.
shows.reviewCon: This praise is for season one. Later seasons are a different, spottier show.

shows.title: The Pitt
shows.description: A high-pressure hospital drama tracking one chaotic ER shift and the people holding it together.
shows.reviewPro: Old-school medical urgency, played over a single ER shift at full volume.
shows.reviewCon: A new show with a hot reputation and a still-short track record.

shows.title: Battlestar Galactica
shows.description: Survivors of a robot apocalypse flee through space while debating what it means to be human.
shows.reviewPro: Space opera that is really about politics, faith, and staying human.
shows.reviewCon: The ending is divisive, and the middle can wander into mythology.

shows.title: Homeland
shows.description: A bipolar CIA officer suspects a rescued POW has been turned into a terrorist asset.
shows.reviewPro: The first season is a taut paranoia machine with a great unstable lead.
shows.reviewCon: It runs long past its best idea. The later years are uneven.

shows.title: Watchmen
shows.description: A remix of the comic that digs into American racism, power, and masked vigilantism.
shows.reviewPro: A fierce, stylish limited series about American power, race, and masks.
shows.reviewCon: It assumes some comic knowledge and makes bold, polarizing swings.

shows.title: Adolescence
shows.description: A contemporary drama centered on teenage life, identity, and the pressures of growing up.
shows.reviewPro: A short, intensely acted portrait of teenage pressure that landed as an event.
shows.reviewCon: Bleak and claustrophobic, with little relief once it gets going.

shows.title: Louie
shows.description: Louis C.K.'s semi-autobiographical comedy about stand-up, parenting, and awkward encounters.
shows.reviewPro: Loose, melancholy stand-up storytelling that widened what a comedy could be.
shows.reviewCon: Hard to separate from Louis C.K.'s later public disgrace.

shows.title: Hacks
shows.description: A legendary comic and a young writer forge a prickly partnership in the Vegas comedy world.
shows.reviewPro: A prickly mentor comedy whose two leads make every insult count.
shows.reviewCon: Showbiz insider jokes and a slow thaw. The spark is the relationship.

shows.title: Peaky Blinders
shows.description: A post-WWI Birmingham gang rises from the streets into organized crime and politics.
shows.reviewPro: Style, violence, and ambition, set to a soundtrack that does half the work.
shows.reviewCon: The myth-making gets repetitive, and historical looseness is part of the deal.

shows.title: BoJack Horseman
shows.description: An animated washed-up sitcom horse confronts depression, fame, and whether people can change.
shows.reviewPro: The saddest, sharpest cartoon about fame, depression, and accountability.
shows.reviewCon: It goes to very dark places. The animal gags are not the real subject.

shows.title: Happy Valley
shows.description: A Yorkshire police sergeant hunts criminals while protecting her family from old wounds.
shows.reviewPro: Grounded, tense, and deeply human crime drama with a formidable lead.
shows.reviewCon: The crimes are brutal, and the show does not look away.

shows.title: Broad City
shows.description: Two best friends bounce through New York in a chaotic, affectionate comedy of millennial life.
shows.reviewPro: Friendship is the love story: silly, specific, and full of New York joy.
shows.reviewCon: The stoner-hangout vibe is the show. Plot is optional.

shows.title: Twin Peaks: The Return
shows.description: David Lynch revisits Twin Peaks decades later in a surreal, unsettling continuation.
shows.reviewPro: A late Lynch epic: eighteen hours of dream logic, dread, and beauty.
shows.reviewCon: Not a cozy reunion. Abstraction and patience are required.

shows.title: House of Cards
shows.description: A ruthless politician and his wife climb Washington's ladder through manipulation and murder.
shows.reviewPro: The early seasons are a sleek, nasty Washington power fantasy.
shows.reviewCon: Later seasons collapse, and the lead's scandal hangs over the show.

shows.title: Normal People
shows.description: Two Irish teens fall into an intense, on-and-off romance from school through university.
shows.reviewPro: An intimate, beautifully acted romance that understands awkward desire.
shows.reviewCon: Very little happens. Mood, sex, and miscommunication carry it.

shows.title: Parks and Recreation
shows.description: An earnest parks official and her quirky colleagues try to make a small town better.
shows.reviewPro: Optimistic workplace comedy that becomes a genuine ensemble classic.
shows.reviewCon: Season one is shaky. The show people love starts a little later.

shows.title: The Good Place
shows.description: A woman wakes in the afterlife and must learn what it actually means to be a good person.
shows.reviewPro: A high-concept comedy that keeps reinventing itself and sticks the landing.
shows.reviewCon: The philosophy and the twists are the fun. Straight-sitcom fans may drift.

shows.title: Downton Abbey
shows.description: An English aristocratic household and its servants navigate class and change before WWII.
shows.reviewPro: Sumptuous upstairs-downstairs soap with a deep bench of characters.
shows.reviewCon: Comfort costume drama. The stakes stay soapy more than severe.

shows.title: Stranger Things
shows.description: 1980s kids in Indiana battle supernatural horrors from a parallel dimension.
shows.reviewPro: A blast of 1980s adventure, friendship, and monster-movie pleasure.
shows.reviewCon: Later seasons stretch the nostalgia, and the scale starts to sag.

shows.title: The Bureau
shows.description: French intelligence officers run covert ops abroad while their private lives unravel at home.
shows.reviewPro: The spy show connoisseurs recommend: procedural, adult, and precise.
shows.reviewCon: French-language, low on glamour, and slow if you want Bond energy.

shows.title: Insecure
shows.description: A young Black woman in L.A. navigates friendship, dating, and figuring herself out.
shows.reviewPro: Specific, funny, and stylish about friendship and dating in Los Angeles.
shows.reviewCon: A character hang, not a plot machine. The lead is not written to be easy.

shows.title: Nathan for You
shows.description: A fake business consultant pitches absurd "improvements" to real small businesses.
shows.reviewPro: Reality comedy as conceptual art. The escalations are hard to believe.
shows.reviewCon: The cringe, and the ethics of the bits, are part of the discomfort.

shows.title: I Think You Should Leave
shows.description: Short, chaotic sketch comedy that escalates ordinary situations into pure nonsense.
shows.reviewPro: Minute-long spirals into social hell. Endlessly rewatchable when it hits.
shows.reviewCon: Sketch hit rate varies, and the volume is shouting-in-a-meeting.

shows.title: Chappelle's Show
shows.description: Dave Chappelle's sketch series that became a cultural phenomenon in the early 2000s.
shows.reviewPro: A sketch show that defined early-2000s comedy and still circulates in clips.
shows.reviewCon: Some material has aged poorly. It is a product of that moment.

shows.title: PEN15
shows.description: Two adult actresses play seventh-graders in a painfully funny middle-school comedy.
shows.reviewPro: Brutally accurate middle-school cringe, played with real tenderness.
shows.reviewCon: Secondhand embarrassment is the point. It can be hard to sit in.

shows.title: Peep Show
shows.description: A British sitcom filmed POV-style as two flatmates spiral through social anxiety and bad choices.
shows.reviewPro: The best British sitcom about anxiety, with the camera stuck in their heads.
shows.reviewCon: The leads are pathetic on purpose. Warmth is scarce.

shows.title: RuPaul's Drag Race
shows.description: Drag queens compete in challenges and runways for the crown of America's Next Drag Superstar.
shows.reviewPro: The competition show that built a canon: runway, wit, and heart.
shows.reviewCon: Long seasons and franchise fatigue. The early years look cheaper.

shows.title: Slow Horses
shows.description: Misfit MI5 agents in a dead-end department stumble into real, dangerous spy work.
shows.reviewPro: A rumpled spy story that is actually funny and actually tense.
shows.reviewCon: The jokes are dry and British. The team is unglamorous by design.

shows.title: The Thick of It
shows.description: A blistering British political satire about spin, incompetence, and verbal warfare.
shows.reviewPro: Political satire at full volume, with a spin doctor who flattens the room.
shows.reviewCon: The shouting and the jargon are the style. It is not a gentle farce.

shows.title: Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown
shows.description: Bourdain travels the world through food, culture, and the stories people tell at the table.
shows.reviewPro: Travel television with curiosity, politics, and real respect for the table.
shows.reviewCon: Episodic wandering, not a plot. The tone can turn melancholy.

shows.title: Mare of Easttown
shows.description: A small-town Pennsylvania detective investigates a murder while her own life falls apart.
shows.reviewPro: A grounded murder mystery anchored by a lead performance at full strength.
shows.reviewCon: Grim small-town crime, more ache than puzzle-box mystery.

shows.title: The Rehearsal
shows.description: Nathan Fielder builds elaborate rehearsals to help people practice high-stakes real-life moments.
shows.reviewPro: Ambitious comedy that starts as a stunt and turns existential.
shows.reviewCon: The artifice, and the ethics questions, are the show. It gets strange.

shows.title: The Handmaid's Tale
shows.description: In a theocratic dystopia, fertile women are forced into reproductive slavery.
shows.reviewPro: The first season is a visceral, well-made warning that landed in the culture.
shows.reviewCon: Later seasons repeat the misery. Plenty of people stopped after the peak.

shows.title: Ozark
shows.description: A financial advisor launders cartel money in the Missouri Ozarks and drags his family under.
shows.reviewPro: A propulsive crime soap with a strong sense of place and escalation.
shows.reviewCon: The logic gets pulpy, and the grimness stacks without much relief.

shows.title: Anthony Bourdain: No Reservations
shows.description: Bourdain's earlier travel series eating his way through cities and cultures worldwide.
shows.reviewPro: The earlier, looser Bourdain: hunger, humor, and cities off the postcard.
shows.reviewCon: Rougher production, and it overlaps the later series in spirit.

shows.title: The Shield
shows.description: A corrupt strike-team cop and his crew blur every line while policing L.A.
shows.reviewPro: The antihero cop show that made prestige television feel dangerous.
shows.reviewCon: An early-2000s look, and the crew's brutality is the subject.

shows.title: Beef (Season 1)
shows.description: A road-rage encounter spirals into an obsession that consumes two strangers' lives.
shows.reviewPro: A vicious, funny spiral about rage, class, and people who cannot let go.
shows.reviewCon: Stressful on purpose. The pettiness curdles into darkness.

shows.title: Squid Game
shows.description: Desperate contestants play deadly children's games for a massive cash prize in South Korea.
shows.reviewPro: A global hit with a clean, brutal premise and sharp production.
shows.reviewCon: The violence is the hook, and later seasons chase the original shock.

shows.title: Barry
shows.description: A hitman takes an acting class and discovers he might prefer the stage to murder.
shows.reviewPro: A hitman comedy that becomes a serious show about talent and harm.
shows.reviewCon: The tone shifts are whiplash. Funnier, then much darker.

shows.title: The Bear
shows.description: A fine-dining chef inherits his family's chaotic Chicago sandwich shop and tries to save it.
shows.reviewPro: Kitchen chaos as a character study. The anxiety is the aesthetic.
shows.reviewCon: Stressful to watch. Shouting, debt, and grief are the recipe.

shows.title: Ted Lasso
shows.description: An relentlessly optimistic American coaches a struggling English soccer club.
shows.reviewPro: A sincere sports comedy that made kindness feel like a plot engine.
shows.reviewCon: Later seasons get preachier. The niceness is not ironic.

shows.title: Somebody Somewhere
shows.description: A woman returns to Kansas and finds unexpected community, grief, and belonging.
shows.reviewPro: Small, humane, and funny, about grief and finding your people.
shows.reviewCon: Very quiet. If you need plot momentum, this will feel still.

shows.title: Modern Family
shows.description: Three related households collide in a warm mockumentary sitcom about contemporary family life.
shows.reviewPro: A broad, sturdy family sitcom with a deep bench of comic actors.
shows.reviewCon: Later seasons coast, and the mockumentary format gets familiar.

shows.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia
shows.description: Five narcissistic friends run a dive bar and invent new ways to be terrible people.
shows.reviewPro: The longest-running joke about terrible people, still finding new lows.
shows.reviewCon: There is no one to root for. That is the contract, for a lot of seasons.

shows.title: The Good Wife
shows.description: A politician's wife returns to law practice after a public sex scandal destroys their life.
shows.reviewPro: A sharp legal procedural that is secretly a great show about power.
shows.reviewCon: Case-of-the-week shape, and it runs long enough to sag.

shows.title: How To with John Wilson
shows.description: John Wilson wanders New York with a camera, turning mundane how-tos into odd human portraits.
shows.reviewPro: A tiny New York essay film disguised as a how-to. Tender and weird.
shows.reviewCon: It meanders by design. Not a joke-machine comedy.

shows.title: The Queen's Gambit
shows.description: An orphaned chess prodigy rises through the male-dominated 1960s chess world while fighting addiction.
shows.reviewPro: A stylish, addictive limited series about genius, loneliness, and chess.
shows.reviewCon: The sports-movie beats are familiar, and the world is very sleek.

shows.title: Better Things
shows.description: A single-mom actress juggles daughters, career, and the mess of everyday life.
shows.reviewPro: A loosely plotted life comedy that is warm, rude, and specific.
shows.reviewCon: Episodes wander. The pleasure is texture, not a tight arc.

shows.title: Justified
shows.description: A U.S. Marshal returns to Kentucky and crosses paths with criminals who know him too well.
shows.reviewPro: Elmore Leonard energy: dialogue, grudges, and a villain people quote.
shows.reviewCon: A case-of-the-week frame sits around the better serialized stretch.

shows.title: Planet Earth
shows.description: Landmark nature documentary series capturing wildlife and landscapes across the globe.
shows.reviewPro: The nature series that reset the standard for footage and awe.
shows.reviewCon: Documentary spectacle, not a story with characters to follow.

shows.title: The Great British Baking Show
shows.description: Amateur bakers compete in a tent with cakes, pastry, and polite British tension.
shows.reviewPro: The nicest competition on television. Real tension, no cruelty.
shows.reviewCon: Low stakes by design. Cozy, not gripping.

shows.title: Shogun
shows.description: An English sailor washes into feudal Japan and is pulled into a war for the shogunate.
shows.reviewPro: An epic, immersive limited series with politics, language, and scale.
shows.reviewCon: A large cast and a deliberate pace. It asks you to settle in.

shows.title: Reservation Dogs
shows.description: Indigenous teens on a reservation scheme, grieve, and chase a way out—or a way through.
shows.reviewPro: Funny, grief-struck, and formally free. A landmark of Indigenous storytelling.
shows.reviewCon: The tone shifts from silly to spiritual. The plot is a loose weave.

shows.title: Dexter
shows.description: A blood-spatter analyst moonlights as a serial killer who only targets other killers.
shows.reviewPro: A killer premise and a magnetic lead, especially in the early seasons.
shows.reviewCon: It overstays badly. The later years are a well-known letdown.

shows.title: Baby Reindeer
shows.description: A comedian is stalked after a small kindness, in a raw story drawn from real events.
shows.reviewPro: A raw, uncomfortable limited series about obsession and the stories we tell.
shows.reviewCon: Harrowing, and the real-life echoes became a public controversy.

shows.title: Eastbound & Down
shows.description: A washed-up MLB pitcher returns home as a gym teacher and refuses to accept obscurity.
shows.reviewPro: Vanity, jokes, and American delusion, played at full volume.
shows.reviewCon: The lead is repulsive on purpose. The volume never drops.

shows.title: Catastrophe
shows.description: A fling becomes a relationship when an American and an Irish woman get unexpectedly pregnant.
shows.reviewPro: A rom-com for adults: sharp, rude, and honest about staying together.
shows.reviewCon: Short and spiky. If you want swooning, this is more of a spar.

shows.title: The Night Of
shows.description: A young man accused of murder navigates Rikers and a grinding New York criminal case.
shows.reviewPro: A sober, gripping limited series about a case grinding through the system.
shows.reviewCon: Bleak and procedural. The night itself is only the beginning.

shows.title: Station Eleven
shows.description: After a flu collapses civilization, a traveling theater troupe and survivors cling to art and memory.
shows.reviewPro: A post-collapse story about art and memory that stays surprisingly gentle.
shows.reviewCon: If you want grim survival horror, the tenderness may throw you.

shows.title: The Diplomat
shows.description: A U.S. ambassador to the U.K. juggles crises, marriage, and Washington power games.
shows.reviewPro: A glossy political thriller with snap, banter, and a fun central marriage.
shows.reviewCon: Closer to a smart soap than to an idealistic civics lesson.

shows.title: House
shows.description: A brilliant, abrasive diagnostician solves medical mysteries no one else can.
shows.reviewPro: A medical-mystery machine built on a genuinely great comic performance.
shows.reviewCon: The formula repeats, and the misanthropy is the brand.

shows.title: Halt and Catch Fire
shows.description: Ambitious misfits chase the next computing revolution through the 1980s and '90s.
shows.reviewPro: A slow-burn period drama about ambition that found its stride late.
shows.reviewCon: The first season is the hard part. The reputation is mostly the later years.

shows.title: Community
shows.description: A disbarred lawyer joins a study group at a ridiculous community college.
shows.reviewPro: Meta sitcom joy when it is locked in. The study group is the point.
shows.reviewCon: Behind-the-scenes turmoil shows. Some seasons feel like a different show.

shows.title: The OA
shows.description: A blind woman returns with her sight and a story of captivity, near-death, and another dimension.
shows.reviewPro: A sincere, strange mystery about trauma, belief, and other worlds.
shows.reviewCon: It asks for a leap, and it was canceled before it could answer itself.

shows.title: Gilmore Girls
shows.description: A mother and daughter navigate life, love, and witty banter in a quirky Connecticut town.
shows.reviewPro: Fast talk, small-town comfort, and a mother-daughter bond as the engine.
shows.reviewCon: The quirky banter never lets up. Love it, or find it exhausting.

shows.title: Scandal
shows.description: A D.C. fixer and her team manage crises for the powerful while hiding plenty of their own.
shows.reviewPro: Addictive network soap: speeches, twists, and a fixer in total command.
shows.reviewCon: It jumps the shark with enthusiasm. Logic is not the attraction.
